name: Pacing and platform rules
summary: The caps per platform, the spacing between sends, links and hashtags, and the signs that mean stop.

nodes.title: The caps table
nodes.body:
- X: about 2 replies per person a day; 1 to 3 originals.
- Bluesky: 1 original a day; replies as people talk to the owner.
- Reddit: answers only where the sub allows them; at most 3 posts about the app a day, 2 hours apart.
- `python playbook/audit.py today` against this table.

nodes.title: Space the sends
nodes.sub: Never empty a cap in one burst
nodes.body:
- 30 to 90 seconds between replies; minutes between originals.
- Keep quiet hours in the owner's time zone.

nodes.title: Any warning signs?
nodes.body:
- A post removed by moderators, a warning from the platform, a rate-limit page.
- People asking who runs the account: answer honestly (flow ground-rules).

nodes.title: Stop and tell the owner
nodes.sub: No more sends on that platform this round
nodes.body: Report what happened, where, and the link. The owner decides when to resume.

nodes.title: Links, sparingly
nodes.body:
- Organic replies carry no links unless the thread asks for one.
- Originals carry at most one, only when the link is the point.

nodes.title: Hashtags
nodes.sub: Two at most on X and Bluesky
nodes.body:
- X and Bluesky: 0 to 2. LinkedIn: up to 3. Instagram, YouTube, TikTok: up to 5.
- No emoji walls.

nodes.title: Promo again in the same place
nodes.sub: Earn it with posts that aren't promos
nodes.body:
- A post about the owner's app in a place where that app was already promoted waits until the account's last 4 posts on that platform include no promo.
- QC filter new-post-rule enforces it.

nodes.sub: Inside the caps, no warning signs
